inputs.prompt: ONE original squat biped furnace automaton, the Quenchbell Mortar, facing screen LEFT in elevated three-quarter view. Keep the dark iron and worn brass riveted body, the round furnace belly with a glowing orange barred grille, the coiled brass pipes and small canisters, the ONE giant short wide mortar barrel mounted on top with a glowing orange rim, its mouth pointing up toward screen left, the ONE jointed loading arm ending in a round dark shell ball with glowing orange seams, held out toward screen left, and EXACTLY TWO thick jointed legs with wide splayed brass feet. No crew and no extra legs or arms. Preserve the mortar, the shell arm, the furnace belly and the squat proportions. Hunker down: the legs spread and bend, lowering the furnace belly close to the ground, the mortar levels out and the shell arm tucks in against the body, then hold the low braced crouch. No firing and no return to the ready height. Locked orthographic camera, fixed scale and centred body. Keep the whole mortar barrel, the shell arm and both feet within frame. The background is perfectly flat saturated BLUE throughout, no gradients or changes of hue. The blue background stays the same flat saturated blue in every frame and never darkens, flashes or changes colour. No scenery, floor shadow, camera motion, zoom, muzzle flash, fire, smoke clouds, sparks, shells in flight, motion trails, particles or extra limbs; only faint steam wisps at the back pipes, and the grille, rim and shell seams keep only their steady glow. The machine moves only at its joints; the barrel stays rigid.
